lines.text: SBA1 - Running a stakeholder discovery conversation
A request such as 'build me a dashboard' is not a requirement. If you start building before discovering the decision, audience, definitions
and constraints, you can deliver exactly what was asked and still solve the wrong problem.
Prepare and conduct a structured discovery conversation that uncovers business decision, audience, current process, metric definitions, scope,
data/freshness, constraints, success criteria, owner and next step.
Course 1 business-question thinking and basic report experience. No formal Business Analyst qualification is assumed.
5. New words before we use them
Stakeholder: Person/group affected by or accountable for the decision/solution. Elicitation: Structured process of drawing out needs, rules, constraints and
context. Acceptance criterion: Observable condition showing that a requirement/deliverable is acceptable.
VISUAL/SOURCE ROUTE: Required visual: Passionate Business Analyst stakeholder interview - 0:00 overview, 1:56 three steps, 8:23 pro tips. Microsoft report-r
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report. Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
Discovery funnel: start with the decision and audience, then narrow through definitions, constraints, evidence, open questions and acceptance. The
requested output is only a proposed format until the decision it supports is clear.
Teacher demonstration - do this once with me, then close the example before your fresh task.
Ask the decision first: 'What decision should this help you make, and how often?' Avoid beginning with chart types.
Identify audience/owner: who uses it, who approves definitions, who acts on the result?
Understand current process and pain: what do they do today, where does it break, what is the cost/risk?
Clarify metric/filters/grain/freshness and examples. Ask what 'sales', 'active customer' or 'late' specifically mean.
Close by restating scope, unanswered questions, success/acceptance criteria, owner and next action. Send the summary for confirmation.
8. What you should see / be able to say
A one-page discovery brief that another analyst can read without guessing the decision or definitions.
The conversation converts a feature request into decision + evidence + constraints + acceptance. Professional upgrade: Strong discovery is concise and
iterative. Use examples, playback/confirmation and explicit decision ownership. A workshop or follow-up may be needed when multiple business areas define
1. Ask only 'what columns/charts do you want?'. | 2. Accept ambiguous KPI names. | 3. Interview only the loudest executive and skip actual
users/owners. | 4. Leave meeting without written confirmation or unanswered-question list.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
Use six anchors: decision, user, current process, definition, constraint/data, acceptance. If one is blank, ask one focused follow-up. Save the genuine
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh case: Operations asks for a 'delivery performance dashboard by tomorrow'. Write 12 discovery questions and a confirmed decision brief.
Every question has a purpose; brief includes decision, user, KPI definition owner, scope, freshness, constraint, acceptance and next step.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain why 'What chart do you want?' is usually too early.
Save your questions/brief first. Changed retry uses a Finance request for 'profit by customer' with an unclear cost-allocation definition.
Discovery agenda + 12 questions + playback summary + open-questions/owners + acceptance criteria + explain-back. After saving evidence, continue
SBA2 - Challenging a bad request professionally
Senior analysts are not order takers. A requested metric, chart or deadline can be misleading, impossible or harmful. The job is to protect
the decision without turning the conversation into 'analyst versus stakeholder'.
Challenge a weak request by acknowledging the goal, identifying the concrete risk, showing evidence/assumption, offering viable options and
asking the correct decision owner to choose.
SBA1 discovery and ability to explain data/metric limitations simply.
5. New words before we use them
Pushback: Professional challenge to a request because of risk, feasibility or decision quality. Trade-off: What is gained and sacrificed by choosing one
option. Decision owner: Person accountable for choosing among legitimate business trade-offs.
VISUAL/SOURCE ROUTE: Book-led; Microsoft BI business-alignment guidance reinforces solution-oriented business/technical discussions.
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report. Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
Request-to-decision translation: separate the stakeholder request from the underlying business decision, then expose risk/constraint, explain why the
literal request may mislead, propose a safer alternative and name the decision owner.
Teacher demonstration - do this once with me, then close the example before your fresh task.
Acknowledge goal: leadership wants to identify performance differences.
State risk without accusation: raw revenue may mostly reflect territory/account mix and can mislabel strong/weak performance.
Show a small control: revenue per active account and territory potential tell a materially different story for two reps.
Offer options: raw revenue as one context metric; normalized comparison; or a two-part scorecard with explicit limitations.
Ask the accountable Sales leader to approve the comparison rule and document the final decision.
8. What you should see / be able to say
Pushback that protects analysis quality while preserving stakeholder trust and momentum.
You object to the decision risk, not to the person, and provide a path forward. Professional upgrade: Good pushback is early, specific and reversible where
possible. Escalate only when risk/ownership demands it; preserve a decision log when material definitions or controls are changed.
1. 'No, that metric is wrong.' | 2. Hide behind technical jargon. | 3. Agree publicly then quietly change the requirement. | 4. Offer five options but
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
Use sentence frame: 'I understand the goal is __. The risk with __ is __ because __. We can do A or B; the trade-off is __. Who should approve the
choice?' Save the genuine attempt before review.
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh case: Product asks you to remove refunded orders because 'they make conversion look bad'. Write a professional response and two alternatives.
Response names business goal, risk/evidence, options/trade-offs, decision owner and documented outcome.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain the difference between challenging a stakeholder and challenging a decision assumption.
Attempt first. Changed retry challenges an impossible same-day deadline without saying only 'we need more time'.
Written pushback + alternative options + trade-off/owner + decision log entry + explain-back. After saving evidence, continue to SBA3.
A senior analyst rarely has one request. If priority is decided by who messages most often, strategic work gets displaced and deadlines
Create a transparent priority system using value/decision impact, urgency/time sensitivity, effort, risk, dependencies and strategic/regulatory
commitment; use scoring as evidence, not fake mathematical truth.
SBA1 decision framing and basic estimation.
5. New words before we use them
Priority: Relative order in which work should receive scarce time/attention. Dependency: Other decision, data, person or work that must happen first or
constrains delivery. WIP: Work in progress; too much simultaneous work increases context switching and delay.
VISUAL/SOURCE ROUTE: Book-led; Microsoft BI strategic planning provides current prioritization/alignment context.
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report. Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
Triage board: compare candidate work by decision impact, urgency, evidence confidence, effort/dependency and non-negotiable risk. Priority is an
explicit trade-off, not whoever asks loudest or whatever is easiest to build.
Teacher demonstration - do this once with me, then close the example before your fresh task.
For each request write decision/consumer and consequence of delay. 'CEO asked' is context, not sufficient benefit description.
Separate hard deadlines (regulatory/contractual) from preference-based urgency.
Estimate effort/risk with rough bands rather than pretending precision you do not have.
Mark dependencies and work already committed. A high-value request blocked on unavailable data may not be executable now.
Publish proposed order and the consequence: 'If urgent request X enters this week, Y moves to next week.' Get the accountable manager to
8. What you should see / be able to say
A priority board that makes both chosen work and displaced work visible.
Priority becomes a transparent management decision rather than a private analyst guess. Professional upgrade: Teams can use RICE, WSJF, impact/effort or
custom frameworks, but senior analysts must expose assumptions, dependencies and decision authority rather than hiding judgment behind decimals.
1. Complex weighted score presented as objective truth. | 2. Urgency equals importance. | 3. Start all high-priority items at once. | 4. Accept new
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
Use five columns: decision/value, deadline, effort/risk, dependency, displacement. Rank only after these are visible. Save the genuine attempt before
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh case: prioritize eight BI requests including a regulatory fix, executive experiment, recurring manual report, broken dashboard and low-value
Top order has defensible reasons; blocked/deferred work is explicit; one incoming urgent request shows displacement.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain why a priority score is a conversation aid rather than a scientific measurement.
Attempt first. Changed retry adds a production incident halfway through the week and requires reprioritization.
Priority matrix + assumptions + dependency/WIP notes + displaced-work communication + explain-back. After saving evidence, continue to SBA4.
SBA4 - Separating observation, inference and recommendation
A chart can prove that two values moved together; it usually cannot prove why. Mixing observation, interpretation and advice makes
analyses sound more certain than the evidence supports.
Label observations, interpretations/hypotheses and recommendations separately; test alternative explanations; avoid causal claims that
5. New words before we use them
Observation: Statement directly supported by measured data under stated definitions. Inference: Interpretation/hypothesis drawn from observations and
assumptions. Recommendation: Proposed action based on evidence, objectives and trade-offs. Causality: Claim that changing one factor causes another
outcome, requiring stronger evidence than correlation alone.
VISUAL/SOURCE ROUTE: Recommended storytelling visual later in SBA5; this lesson is evidence-language led.
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report. Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
Evidence ladder: Observation = directly supported by data; Inference = plausible interpretation with alternatives/assumptions; Recommendation =
action proposed for a decision. Never let a recommendation masquerade as observed fact.
Teacher demonstration - do this once with me, then close the example before your fresh task.
Observation: conversion fell from 4.8% to 4.1% after 15 June under the same metric definition.
Do not jump to 'price increase caused the decline'. List possible causes: traffic mix, campaign shift, outage, seasonality, competitor action,
Check available controls/segments/timing and record which explanations are supported, contradicted or still unknown.
Inference: the timing and segment pattern make pricing a plausible contributor, but the current observational data does not isolate its causal
Recommendation: run a controlled pricing test or inspect the strongest competing explanation first, with owner/success criterion.
8. What you should see / be able to say
A decision note where facts, interpretations and actions can be challenged independently.
Uncertainty in explanation does not prevent action; it changes the action and the language. Professional upgrade: Executives need confidence calibrated to
evidence. Use causal language only when design/evidence supports it; otherwise use 'associated with', 'consistent with', 'likely contributor' and explicit next
1. Trend = cause. | 2. Use 'proves' when analysis is observational. | 3. List uncertainty so vaguely that no action is possible. | 4.
Recommendation presented as another observed fact.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
Color/tag every sentence O, I or R. If an inference has no alternative explanation considered, add at least two. Save the genuine attempt before review.
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh case: churn rose after a support-policy change. Write 4 observations, 3 competing inferences, 2 tests and one cautious recommendation.
Observations are measurable; inferences cite evidence/assumptions; recommendation matches uncertainty and decision urgency.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain why 'A happened before B' is not enough to say A caused B.
Attempt first. Changed retry analyzes delivery delay and customer complaints with a hidden holiday-season confounder.
O/I/R tagged memo + alternative hypotheses + test/recommendation + explain-back. After saving evidence, continue to SBA5.
Write a concise decision-first executive summary with headline, evidence, implication, recommendation, uncertainty/limitation and explicit
5. New words before we use them
Executive summary: Concise decision-oriented synthesis of situation, evidence, implications and next actions. So what: Business consequence/meaning of a
finding. Ask: Specific approval, decision, resource or action requested from the audience.
VISUAL/SOURCE ROUTE: Recommended: storytelling with data 10th anniversary session (2025) for audience/story emphasis; current Power BI
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report. Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
Inverted pyramid: lead with the decision-relevant headline, then the minimum evidence, implication, uncertainty/trade-off and decision ask. Executives
should understand what needs deciding before they reach implementation detail.
Teacher demonstration - do this once with me, then close the example before your fresh task.
Decision/headline: 'Renewal risk is concentrated in two enterprise segments; approve targeted retention test this month.'
Evidence: state 2-3 numbers with period/definition context, not a table dump.
Implication: quantify or clearly describe business consequence if no action is taken.
Recommendation: one primary action plus owner/timing.
Uncertainty/limitation: identify the material caveat only. End with the explicit ask/next decision.
8. What you should see / be able to say
A summary readable in under a minute that preserves evidence, uncertainty and action.
The summary follows the audience's decision path rather than the analyst's analysis chronology. Professional upgrade: Use layered communication: headline
and ask first; supporting visuals/definitions behind it. AI-generated narratives may accelerate drafting, but you remain responsible for factual accuracy, scope
1. Start with 'I analyzed 12 tables...' | 2. Paste every KPI. | 3. Recommendation hidden in last paragraph. | 4. No limitation, or a paragraph of
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
Use six lines: decision/headline; evidence 1; evidence 2; implication; recommendation; ask + material caveat. Save the genuine attempt before review.
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh case: write a 120-word executive summary from a regional service-performance snapshot with one data limitation.
Reviewer can answer 'what happened / why care / what do / what decide / what caveat?' without opening supporting pages.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain why an executive summary is not a shorter version of your methodology section.
Attempt first. Changed retry reduces your summary to 80 words for a CFO while preserving decision and caveat.
120-word summary + 80-word transfer + supporting evidence references + explain-back. After saving evidence, continue to SBA6.
Hiding uncertainty creates false confidence; flooding stakeholders with every caveat makes analysis unusable. Senior communication
shows how uncertainty could change the decision.
Present uncertainty through known/unknown, data quality/freshness, range/scenario or confidence language; connect uncertainty to decision
SBA4 evidence-language discipline and basic percentage/range understanding.
5. New words before we use them
Uncertainty: What is not known precisely about a measurement, estimate, explanation or future outcome. Scenario range: Set of plausible outcomes under
explicit assumptions. Decision sensitivity: Whether reasonable uncertainty could change which action is preferred.
VISUAL/SOURCE ROUTE: Book-led. Current Microsoft BI strategy/business-alignment guidance supports transparent communication; statistical method belongs
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report. Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
Fog map: mark what is known, unknown, assumed and estimated; show a plausible range or scenarios when possible; state which uncertainty could
change the decision and when/how evidence will be updated.
Teacher demonstration - do this once with me, then close the example before your fresh task.
Best current estimate: 180 analyst hours saved/month based on 12 sampled workflows.
Known limitations: sample is concentrated in two teams; manual-time estimates are self-reported.
Scenario range: conservative 120, base 180, optimistic 230 hours using explicit adoption/volume assumptions.
Decision sensitivity: project still clears the approval threshold at 120 hours, so uncertainty does not change go/no-go-but affects staffing/benefit
Update plan: measure actual time for four weeks after launch and replace estimate with observed range.
8. What you should see / be able to say
Uncertainty is visible, proportionate and tied to how the decision could change.
You do not pretend precision, but you still give the decision owner a usable recommendation. Professional upgrade: Use statistical intervals when the method
supports them and the audience can use them; otherwise transparent scenarios/ranges may communicate decision risk more honestly than decorative
1. Give one decimal-point forecast as fact. | 2. Say 'data may be imperfect' without impact. | 3. Use confidence interval jargon you cannot explain.
| 4. List caveats but no plan to reduce uncertainty.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
Write: estimate; biggest uncertainty; plausible range/scenarios; does it change decision?; what evidence will update it? Save the genuine attempt
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh case: estimate churn reduction from a proposed retention campaign using three scenarios and a decision threshold.
Assumptions are explicit; range is internally coherent; language does not imply stronger evidence than available; update plan has owner/timing.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain the difference between being uncertain and being unable to recommend.
Attempt first. Changed retry introduces stale/incomplete data and asks whether the recommendation still holds.
Uncertainty table + scenario/threshold note + update plan + explain-back. After saving evidence, continue to SBA7.
SBA7 - Recommendations tied to business decisions
A recommendation like 'monitor this KPI' often avoids making a decision. Strong recommendations specify an action, owner, timing,
trade-off and what evidence will determine whether to continue, change or stop.
Turn findings into decision-ready recommendations with action, owner, timing, expected impact, risk/trade-off, success measure and
5. New words before we use them
Decision rule: Pre-agreed criterion that determines what action to take when evidence reaches a threshold. Reversible action: Action that can be
tested/undone with limited cost, making experimentation safer. Success measure: Metric/control used to judge whether the recommendation achieved the
VISUAL/SOURCE ROUTE: Book-led; storytelling video supports action-oriented communication.
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report. Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
Action contract: a recommendation is not complete until it has action, accountable owner, timing, expected direction of impact, risk/trade-off, success
measure and review/stop condition. Monitoring without a decision rule is not an action plan.
Teacher demonstration - do this once with me, then close the example before your fresh task.
Finding: South enterprise churn is 3.1 points above comparable regions, concentrated in onboarding months 1-2.
Decision: whether to allocate two customer-success specialists for a six-week onboarding intervention.
Recommendation: run intervention for new South enterprise accounts; owner Head of CS; launch 1 Oct; cap resource at two FTE-equivalents.
Expected impact/trade-off: target >=1.5-point reduction; cost is diverted CS capacity; guardrail complaints/SLA must not worsen.
Review after six weeks. Continue/scale only if churn proxy/leading measures and guardrails meet the agreed rule; otherwise stop/adjust.
8. What you should see / be able to say
A recommendation the decision owner can approve, reject or modify without asking 'what exactly should we do?'
Action is bounded and measurable, with explicit trade-offs and review. Professional upgrade: Prefer small reversible experiments when uncertainty is material
and delay is tolerable. Use stronger commitments when evidence, regulation or operational urgency justifies them.
1. 'We recommend monitoring.' | 2. No owner/deadline. | 3. Impact claim exceeds evidence. | 4. Success KPI has no baseline/threshold.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
Use template: We recommend [action] by [owner] by [time] because [evidence]. Expect [impact]. Risk/trade-off [x]. Measure [y], guardrail [z],
review/stop rule [date/threshold]. Save the genuine attempt before review.
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh case: high delivery cancellations in two cities. Write one reversible recommendation and one larger strategic option.
Each option has owner, timing, impact hypothesis, cost/risk, success/guardrail and decision/review rule.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain why a recommendation should be falsifiable/testable rather than just sound sensible.
Attempt first. Changed retry has a lower budget and requires changing the action without changing the business goal.
Decision brief + two recommendation options + success/guardrail/review rules + explain-back. After saving evidence, continue to SBA8.
When Finance says 'official revenue must match ledger' and Sales says 'show live booked revenue', both can be reasonable because they
support different decisions. Combining them into one unlabeled number creates mistrust.
Identify the underlying goals/non-negotiables behind conflicting requests; distinguish definition, scope, timing and policy conflicts; propose
options and route the unresolved trade-off to the correct owner.
SBA1 discovery, SBA2 pushback and SBA3 priority decisions.
5. New words before we use them
Non-negotiable: Constraint that cannot be traded away by the analyst, such as regulatory/accounting/security rule. Conflict log: Record of incompatible
requirements, options, owners and final decision. Source of truth: Authoritative data/definition for a specific governed purpose-not necessarily one universal
VISUAL/SOURCE ROUTE: Microsoft business-alignment guidance is recommended; lesson remains case-led.
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report. Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
Conflict table: list each stakeholder goal, the non-negotiable constraint, the actual point of conflict, viable options and the person authorized to choose
the trade-off. The analyst surfaces conflict; they do not silently invent a compromise.
Teacher demonstration - do this once with me, then close the example before your fresh task.
Write each stakeholder's actual decision: Finance closes accounts; Sales monitors pipeline/bookings daily.
Identify definition/timing conflict: recognized ledger revenue vs booked commercial value. Do not force them into one unlabeled metric.
Mark non-negotiables: Finance close must reconcile to ledger; Sales can use operational leading measure if clearly labeled.
Offer design: two explicitly named metrics/views with definitions and reconciliation bridge, or one executive page with separate
Assign metric-definition owner and document final choice, audience and warning against cross-purpose comparison.
8. What you should see / be able to say
Conflict is resolved or escalated as a business decision; the analyst does not silently choose a winner.
Both requirements are translated to their legitimate decision contexts. Professional upgrade: Enterprise BI often needs governed metric namespaces/purpose
labels and a decision log. Consensus is useful; forced semantic compromise can be dangerous.
1. Average/merge two definitions to make everyone 'happy'. | 2. Let hierarchy alone determine truth when policy says otherwise. | 3. Create two
metrics with same label. | 4. Keep disagreement verbal and forget after release.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
Create conflict table: stakeholder, decision, requirement, why needed, non-negotiable?, conflict type, options, trade-off, decision owner. Save the
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh case: Product wants weekly active users by event activity; Finance wants billable active accounts. Resolve without creating one misleading
Every conflicting definition has decision purpose and owner; chosen labels prevent accidental substitution; unresolved trade-off goes to accountable
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain why two different 'correct' metrics can coexist if they answer different decisions.
Attempt first. Changed retry introduces Privacy's data-minimization constraint against Marketing's detailed segmentation request.
Conflict log + option/trade-off matrix + final definition/owner + explain-back. After saving evidence, continue to SBA9.
SBA9 - Defending your analysis under questioning
A senior review is not a test of confidence. Good analysts can defend evidence, state assumptions, admit what they do not know and
update a conclusion when a valid challenge changes the facts.
Prepare a defense map; answer questions with claim/evidence/limitation; distinguish challenge from new requirement; handle 'I don't know'
professionally; revise conclusions when evidence warrants.
5. New words before we use them
Defense map: Preparation linking each key claim/recommendation to evidence, assumptions, likely challenges and fallback detail. Assumption: Condition
treated as true for the analysis/recommendation but not fully established by direct evidence. Revision trigger: New evidence that would materially change the
VISUAL/SOURCE ROUTE: Storytelling with data is optional visual support for audience-focused presentation; practice is primarily live/role-play writing.
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report. Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
Defense map: link every important claim to evidence, assumption/limitation, likely challenge and revision trigger. A strong defense can say "I do not
know yet" and specify what evidence would change the answer.
Teacher demonstration - do this once with me, then close the example before your fresh task.
List your three strongest claims and the exact evidence/definitions supporting each.
For each, write the strongest plausible challenge: data completeness, comparison group, seasonality, cost or unintended consequence.
Prepare concise answer: direct answer first, evidence second, limitation third. Do not drown the room in methodology unless asked.
If you do not know, say what is unknown, whether it affects the decision and when/how you will verify it.
If a valid challenge breaks an assumption, update the recommendation. Defending analysis does not mean defending every original sentence.
8. What you should see / be able to say
A calm, evidence-linked review where uncertainty and revision improve trust rather than appearing as weakness.
The objective is decision quality, not winning an argument. Professional upgrade: Use an appendix/evidence pack for detail while keeping verbal answers
decision-focused. Record unanswered questions and commitments after the meeting.
1. Answer every question with more charts. | 2. Bluff when you do not know. | 3. Treat criticism as personal disagreement. | 4. Never change
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
Prepare one card per claim: claim; evidence; definition; assumption; likely challenge; concise answer; revision trigger. Save the genuine attempt before
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh case: defend a recommendation to close a low-volume service location against Finance, Operations and Sales questions.
Answers address the question directly, cite evidence/assumption, acknowledge real limitations and define what would change the recommendation.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain why changing your conclusion after better evidence is a strength, not a failed defense.
Attempt first. Changed retry adds one valid data-quality challenge that requires narrowing-not abandoning-the recommendation.
Defense map + 8-question Q&A + revision trigger + follow-up log + explain-back. After saving evidence, continue to SBA10.
SBA10 - Working with engineers, finance, product and operations
Cross-functional teams fail when everyone assumes another team owns definitions, data, deployment or acceptance. Senior analysts
translate business decisions into evidence and contracts that each discipline can act on.
Recognize each partner's common concerns; assign accountable ownership with RACI-like clarity; create handoffs for data, metric and
SBA1, SBA8 and C2-07 collaboration/handoff concepts.
5. New words before we use them
RACI: Responsibility aid: Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed. Acceptance test: Concrete evidence showing the delivered change satisfies the
agreed business/technical requirement. Interface contract: Agreement at a team boundary: data/definition/input/output/owner/failure expectations.
VISUAL/SOURCE ROUTE: Microsoft BI business-alignment guidance is recommended; current PL-300 profile also explicitly expects analyst collaboration with
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report. Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
Handshake contracts: Finance, Product, Operations and Engineering each need explicit inputs, outputs, definitions, owners, deadlines,
failure/escalation rules and acceptance evidence. Cross-functional trust comes from visible contracts, not informal memory.
Teacher demonstration - do this once with me, then close the example before your fresh task.
Finance owns/accountably approves margin definition/accounting treatment; analyst translates it into testable calculation examples.
Data/analytics engineer owns required curated fields/pipeline/model transformations; handoff includes source/grain/key/freshness/sample
Product/Operations explain the decision/workflow and adoption constraints; analyst ensures report/action fits how work is done.
Analyst owns analysis/report interpretation, validation and communication unless organizational roles assign differently.
Create acceptance pack: Finance reconciliation examples, engineering data-quality checks, user decision scenario and owner sign-off.
8. What you should see / be able to say
A cross-functional plan with no invisible ownership gap between business definition, data production and decision use.
Each role receives the context/evidence it needs while one accountable owner remains clear for each decision. Professional upgrade: RACI is useful only
when it clarifies action. Keep it small and pair it with concrete interface/acceptance contracts.
1. RACI with everyone accountable. | 2. Analyst owns accounting definition without Finance approval. | 3. Engineer receives vague 'need
customer data'. | 4. Operations informed only after report launch.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh case: create a cancellation-risk dashboard requiring Product event definitions, Engineering pipeline fields, Finance cost and Operations
Every important deliverable has one accountable owner; handoffs have grain/definition/evidence; acceptance spans technical + business use.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain why ownership is about decisions/deliverables, not job-title hierarchy.
Attempt first. Changed retry removes one source field and requires renegotiating the cross-team acceptance scope.
RACI + data/metric contract + acceptance matrix + explain-back. After saving evidence, continue to SBA11.
SBA11 - Code, review and documentation habits
Senior analyst work must survive handover and review. A correct SQL query hidden in 'final_final_v3.sql' with no definition or validation is
fragile even if the numbers are right today.
Create lightweight professional documentation around SQL/Power Query/Python/BI changes: purpose, input/output grain, assumptions,
validation, version/change log, review comments and reproducible evidence.
Technical modules C2-01 to C2-07; no Git expertise beyond basic repository habits is assumed.
5. New words before we use them
Peer review: Another person checks correctness, clarity, risk and evidence before release. Change log: Record of meaningful changes, reason, date/owner
and possible impact. Reproducibility: Ability for another person/process to recreate the intended result from documented code/config/data assumptions.
VISUAL/SOURCE ROUTE: Book-led; GitHub review tooling is optional implementation detail, not required for the competency.
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report. Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
Change trail: work item -> versioned change/diff -> peer review -> validation -> documentation/change log -> release. Reproducibility means another
person can understand the purpose, inputs, assumptions and checks without tribal knowledge.
Teacher demonstration - do this once with me, then close the example before your fresh task.
README/work-item states business question, source tables, output grain, KPI definitions/assumptions and owner.
Query is readable and avoids unexplained magic constants; comments explain business reasoning or non-obvious choices.
Reviewer checks grain/joins/filters/nulls/date boundaries and compares to an independent control or prior approved result.
Review comment is specific: issue, why it matters, suggested direction or question. Author responds/repairs and saves evidence.
Change log records what changed and downstream impact; released artifact can be traced to the reviewed version.
8. What you should see / be able to say
A small review package another analyst can understand, rerun and challenge.
Correctness evidence and reasoning travel with the code rather than living only in the author's memory. Professional upgrade: Use repository pull
requests/change requests when available, but the core habit is traceable peer review plus reproducible evidence. Protect sensitive data in
1. Comment every obvious SELECT line but not the business rule. | 2. Reviewer says only 'looks good'. | 3. Rename files instead of
version/change control. | 4. Copy sensitive production data into review evidence.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
Document five things: purpose, grain, assumptions, validation, change. Then ask reviewer one specific high-risk question. Save the genuine attempt
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh case: review a junior SQL query that joins monthly targets to order lines and overstates target. Write review comments, corrected design
Review catches grain issue, explains impact without humiliating author, asks for evidence and updates documentation/change log.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain why review is not merely checking syntax or formatting.
Attempt first. Changed retry reviews a pandas transformation with silent coercion and missing exception count.

C2_08 Practical Mastery Check - Protected Review RC4
Open only after a saved genuine attempt; diagnose, close, then solve a changed retry.
Task
Expected reasoning pattern
1
Ask decision/audience, definition of "worst," eligible population/time window, evidence available, costs/risks, constraints, action
capacity and who owns the ranking/action.
2
State the business decision first, define the metric and population/time grain, then name the person who chooses the trade-off.
3
Use an explicit scoring/triage rule; non-negotiable risk/finance/security controls can override a simple score.
4
Observation must be directly supported; inference states an explanation plus alternatives; recommendation states an action
bounded by evidence.
5
Lead with the decision-relevant headline, then only enough evidence, implication, material uncertainty/trade-off and the specific
decision required.
6
Name the unknown, why it matters, current safe decision boundary, evidence owner/timing and what threshold/result would
change the recommendation.
7
Specify the action, accountable owner, when, intended direction of impact, risk/trade-off, success measure and review/stop rule.
8
Keep both governed purposes/definitions visible, propose labeled alternatives or separate metrics, and route the unresolved
policy trade-off to the authorized owner.
9
Tie claim to evidence; state assumptions/causal limits; list likely challenge, what evidence is missing and the revision trigger.
10
Define old/new KPI rule, source/interface change, owner per team, acceptance tests, effective date, rollback/failure path and
communication.
11
Purpose, inputs/outputs/grain, code/query/version, assumptions, validation/reconciliation, reviewer decision, change log and
release evidence.
12
Ask the learner what evidence establishes causality, what alternatives exist and how the wording should change if only
association is known; require a changed retry and teach-back.
Changed retry
Close this review. Solve an equivalent management case in a different domain with new evidence, a stakeholder conflict and
one material uncertainty. Save separately. Module Test remains non-gating.

C2-08 Protected Practice Review
OPEN ONLY AFTER THE MATCHING CASE ATTEMPT
Course 2A - C2-08 Protected Learning
Page 1
HOW TO USE
Compare the quality of your reasoning, evidence and ownership—not exact wording. Preserve your first response. Close this review
before changed retry. If the review gives you language you did not independently produce, that language is not mastery.
CRITICAL FAILURES
Invented facts; causal certainty unsupported by evidence; misleading metric compromise; material uncertainty hidden; no decision
owner; recommendation has no executable action/measure; priority hides displaced work; defense bluffs unknowns; review misses
critical data/grain failure; mentoring simply hands over the answer.

Page 1 - Evidence and decision boundary
Area
Evidence / control
Domain
Marketplace Sellers
Non-negotiable
Finance profitability + Trust fraud/refund risk cannot be hidden
Capacity/constraint
Seller Ops can act on 20 sellers/week
Observed evidence
Seller A: GMV 420,000; refund 8%; fraud flag 18%; contribution margin 16%; on-time ship 92%
Seller B: 360,000; 3%; 5%; 24%; 88%
Seller C: 310,000; 10%; 21%; 13%; 74%
Seller D: 280,000; 2%; 4%; 27%; 96%
Seller E: 250,000; 4%; 7%; 22%; 90%
Material limitations
Fraud outcome lags transactions by up to 14 days (High)
Seller category mix affects return rates (Medium)
No controlled evidence that coaching causes GMV improvement (High)
Required output
A management recommendation that separates observation, inference and recommendation; shows stakeholder trade-offs;
states uncertainty; gives action/owner/measure/review; and identifies missing evidence/owners rather than inventing facts.

Course 2A | C2_08 | Astra Parity RC4
Page 2
Page 2 - Expected reasoning and diagnostic traps
Expected reasoning
GMV-only ranking would favor A/B/C by volume but would hide material Trust/Finance signals; Trust and profitability are explicit
non-negotiables.
Seller C has the highest refund/fraud rates, lowest contribution margin and weakest on-time shipping in this five-seller evidence set; it is a
defensible intervention priority, but do not claim a cause without further evidence.
Seller A combines highest GMV with elevated refund/fraud risk and lower margin than B/D/E; volume does not make the risk disappear.
Seller D is strongest on margin, refund/fraud and on-time shipping in this set; low intervention priority is defensible, but "best seller"
depends on the defined decision.
Fraud lag means current fraud flags may be incomplete; category mix means return-rate comparisons need segmentation before
causal/policy conclusions.
The case contains only five sellers while Ops capacity is 20/week. Do not invent a capacity bottleneck; state whether this sample is
complete and ask for the full intervention population if needed.
Because coaching impact is not controlled, recommend an intervention/measurement plan rather than promising GMV uplift.
Critical traps
Trap
Why it blocks
Single-metric ranking
It can hide explicit finance/risk/policy constraints and answer the wrong decision.
Causal language from observational
evidence
Association/risk score/operational pattern does not establish intervention effect.
Silent stakeholder compromise
The analyst is not authorized to erase a non-negotiable; expose options and decision
owner.
Fake precision
Missing cost, calibration, population or causal evidence must remain uncertainty/open
question.
No owner/review rule
A recommendation without accountable action and evidence review is not an executable
management decision.
